desk.g.balance: Money in your account, not counting open trades.

desk.g.credit: Bonus funds from the broker. They count toward equity but cannot be withdrawn.
desk.g.equity: Balance plus the profit or loss of your open trades: what the account is worth right now.
desk.g.free: Money still available for new trades: equity minus margin.
desk.g.hedging: Every trade is its own position, so you can hold a buy and a sell on the same market.
desk.g.level: Equity divided by margin. Higher is safer. If it falls too low, trades are closed automatically.
desk.g.leverage: Lets you open a trade larger than your margin. 1:100 means $1 of margin controls $100.
desk.g.lot: The trade size unit. 1 lot of EURUSD is 100,000 euros; 0.01 lot is 1,000.
desk.g.margin: Money set aside to keep your open trades running. You get it back when they close.
desk.g.netting: One position per market: a new trade adds to it or reduces it.
desk.g.pip: A small price step used to measure moves: 0.0001 for most currency pairs.
desk.g.pnl: Profit or loss of your open trades at current prices. It becomes real when you close them.
desk.g.sl: A price at which the trade closes by itself to limit your loss.
desk.g.spread: The difference between the Buy and Sell price. It is the cost of opening a trade.
desk.g.swap: A small daily fee or credit for keeping a trade open overnight.
desk.g.tp: A price at which the trade closes by itself to lock in your profit.

desk.og.atm: The strike closest to the current price. These options react most to small moves.
desk.og.be: Where the trade stops losing at expiry: the strike plus the premium for a call, the strike minus the premium for a put.
desk.og.call: An option that gains when the price rises. It pays at expiry if the price ends above the strike.
desk.og.cut: How long until the cut, the moment the option settles. Until then you can close it at the current price.
desk.og.delta: How much the option price moves when the market moves by one unit. It is also a rough chance of ending in the money.
desk.og.expiry: The day the option ends. At the cut time that day it settles by itself: in the money it pays, out of the money it expires worthless.
desk.og.gamma: How fast delta itself changes as the price moves. High near the strike and close to expiry.
desk.og.greeks: Four numbers that show how the option price reacts: to the price (delta, gamma), to time (theta) and to volatility (vega).
desk.og.itm: An option that would pay something if it expired now: a call below the price, a put above it.
desk.og.iv: How much the market expects the price to move, from at-the-money option prices. Higher IV makes options cost more.
desk.og.otm: An option that would pay nothing if it expired now. It is cheaper, and it needs a bigger move to pay.
desk.og.premium: The price of the option. A buyer pays it once, up front, and it is the most the buyer can lose.
desk.og.put: An option that gains when the price falls. It pays at expiry if the price ends below the strike.
desk.og.selling: The seller receives the premium now but needs margin and can lose much more than the premium if the price moves against them.
desk.og.settle: At the cut the option settles in cash by itself, from the average price of the last 30 minutes. In the money pays; out of the money expires worthless.
desk.og.strike: The price the option is measured against. A call pays above it, a put pays below it.
desk.og.theta: How much value the option loses each day as expiry gets closer, if nothing else changes (time decay).
desk.og.vega: How much the option price changes when implied volatility moves by one point.

trader.opt.mm.feesText: An order that trades at once pays the taker fee; an order that waits in the book and then fills earns the maker rebate. Both are per contract and capped at a percentage of the premium. The market maker pays no fees and gets no rebates.
trader.opt.mm.intro: Kalks runs a market maker that quotes a buy and a sell price in every option, so there is always someone to trade with. It trades on the same order book as you, under the same rules.
trader.opt.mm.latency: Latency: the market maker runs inside the trading engine, next to the book. That in-process speed is the only difference from a client order; it gets no other advantage.
trader.opt.mm.lpText: In the last 15 minutes before an expiry's cut, clients can only close positions. As a liquidity provider, the market maker may keep quoting until 1 minute before the cut, so you can still close.
trader.opt.mm.quote1: Its quotes only add liquidity (post-only): it never takes your orders off the book.
trader.opt.mm.quote2: Prices come from the volatility model, with a spread that is wider for short-dated options and shifts with its inventory and risk limits.
trader.opt.mm.quote3: It withdraws its quotes when prices are stale, the market is closed or a dealer pauses it.
trader.opt.mm.rule1: It sends its quotes through the same order entry as clients, with the same checks.
trader.opt.mm.rule2: No priority: orders fill by price, then by time. Nobody is ahead of you at the same price because of who they are.
trader.opt.mm.rule3: No early view: it sees only the public order book and its own orders, like you.
trader.opt.mm.rule4: Its quotes are firm: no last look, no re-pricing after your order arrives.
trader.opt.mm.rule5: Every fill records the market maker's quote, and a nightly replay audit checks it.
